claims.claim: He was born around 313 and died around 398, having been blind since early childhood.
Didymus was anathematized at the Fifth Ecumenical Council in 553 because of his utilization and defense of Origen’s works, which contributed to the loss of many of his writings.
The Commentary on Genesis is one of several Old Testament commentaries Didymus wrote, and scholars think it may represent his earliest work.
The work survived only in fragmentary form because papyrus codices containing it were discovered in 1941 at the Tura site near Cairo, Egypt.
Didymus remained a layman all his life and was a staunch opponent of Arianism and Macedonian teachings.
